text: Dubai Land Department: the government body that registers property, ownership and transactions in Dubai and collects the transfer fee.
Real Estate Regulatory Agency, part of DLD. It regulates developers, brokers, escrow accounts and off-plan projects.
Abu Dhabi Real Estate Centre: registers and regulates property in Abu Dhabi.
A bank account for one project only, where buyers' off-plan payments are held and released to the developer as the building rises.
DLD's interim register for off-plan sales. Your purchase is recorded here before the building is complete.
Sale and Purchase Agreement: the main contract with the developer or seller, covering price, plan and handover terms.
The official record of ownership issued once the property is transferred to you.
DLD's fee on a purchase in Dubai: 4% of the price, paid by the buyer by market convention.
When the developer completes the building and hands over the keys. A large instalment is often due at this point.
A payment plan where part of the price is paid in instalments after you receive the keys.
The yearly fee for maintaining the building and community, charged per square foot of your unit.
The standard resale agreement (MOU) between buyer and seller in Dubai, setting price, deposit and who pays which fees.
No-objection certificate from the developer, needed to transfer a resale or off-plan unit.
Broker Registration Number. Every licensed Dubai broker has one; check it before you deal with them.
Full ownership of the property and land. Foreigners can buy freehold in designated areas.
Inspecting a new unit for defects before or at handover so the developer fixes them.
DLD's official real-estate app: look up projects, developers, brokers and escrow details.
Rent left after service charges, empty weeks, management and maintenance, as a percentage of the price.
